title: Enterprise Onboarding: Escalation, Integration, Health Checks & QBR Playbook
author: Sofia Martinez
summary: A consolidated playbook for enterprise customer onboarding that combines integration runbooks, escalation procedures, regular health checks, and QBR materials. Intended to standardize go‑live, reduce time-to-value, and streamline incident escalation for enterprise accounts.
audience: Customer Success Managers, Solutions Engineers, Support Engineers, Onboarding Project Managers, Account Owners
body:
Overview:

This playbook sets the standard for enterprise onboarding at Redwood Inference. It contains prescriptive checklists for handoffs, an escalation matrix and runbook for production issues, an integration checklist for common customer environments, a curated list of known issues with workarounds, and the artifacts/templates used in Health Checks and Quarterly Business Reviews (QBR).

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-first-successful-request for enterprise customers to <= 7 business days.
- Ensure consistent post‑go‑live monitoring and proactive health checks.
- Provide a low-latency, documented escalation path to resolve Sev1/Sev2 incidents within SLOs.

Scope:
- Applies to all enterprise accounts using Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployments.
- Covers: pre-sales to handoff, integration & connectivity, go‑live checklist, post‑go‑live health checks, escalation process, QBR cadence & materials.

Ownership & Roles:
- Customer Success (CSM): overall onboarding owner, QBR lead, coordinates internal and customer stakeholders.
- Solutions Engineering (SE): technical lead for integration, runbook authoring, and validation of performance.
- Support Engineering (Support): primary oncall for incident triage and problem resolution.
- Account Executive (AE): commercial point of contact until contract is fully active.
- Product/Infra Eng: escalation targets for platform bugs and capacity issues.

Onboarding Phases & Checklists:
1) Pre-handoff (Sales -> CS):
- Confirm contract, billing entity, and deployment mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private).
- Collect customer technical contacts, network contacts, and required IP allowlists.
- Share onboarding timeline and staffing plan.

2) Integration Kickoff (Day 0–2):
- Kickoff agenda: participants, success criteria, data classification, target workload patterns, and peak QPS.
- Provide customer with API keys (or deploy private control plane credentials) following KMS/HSM guidance.
- Verify network connectivity:
  - Hosted: Ensure customer can egress to api.redwood.ai on ports 443.
  - Dedicated/Private: Validate VPC peering, firewall rules, and VPN tunnels.
- Integration checklist (sample):
  - Obtain sample prompts and expected outputs.
  - Verify authentication flow (API key rotation test).
  - Run sample inference at 1 RPS and validate output shape & latency.
  - Confirm streaming, function/tool calling, or embedding flows as required.

3) Performance Validation (Day 3–5):
- Execute load plan: 1 RPS -> 5 RPS -> target RPS / burst policy. Monitor latency and error rate.
- Validate representative workloads: sequence length distribution, concurrency, and batch sizes.
- Capture baseline metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, error rate.
- If Dedicated: confirm reserved capacity meets expected concurrency; run failover test (regional fallback).

4) Go‑Live & Post Go‑Live (Day 5–7):
- Go‑live checklist: DNS, API keys swapped to production, usage quotas configured, alerting enabled, and a 72-hour hypercare schedule.
- Hypercare: daily syncs for first 3 days, then alternate-day check-ins until stable.

Escalation Playbook (Incident Handling):
- Severity Definitions:
  - Sev1 (Critical): Customer-facing outage or 50%+ error rate / total loss of inference capability. Target TTL: 1 hour to initial mitigation, 4 hours to resolution or permanent workaround.
  - Sev2 (High): Severe degradation impacting core functionality (e.g., latency > p99 SLO x 3). Target TTL: 2 hours to mitigation, 24 hours to resolution.
  - Sev3 (Medium): Partial loss or degraded performance with a clear workaround. Target TTL: 24 hours to resolution.
  - Sev4 (Low): Informational or enhancement requests. Target TTL: next-sprint planning.

- Escalation Matrix (contact sequence):
| Phase | Action | Primary Owner | Secondary Owner | Slack Channel | Pager |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---:|
| Triage (0–15m) | Acknowledge & classify severity | Support Tier 1 | CSM | #support-triage | No |
| Initial Mitigation (15–60m) | Apply workaround, rate-limit or shift routing | Support Eng | SE | #support-incident | Yes for Sev1/2 |
| Engineering Escalation (60–180m) | Involve runtime/product owners, retrieve logs & traces | Eng-Serving-Runtime | Eng-Infra | #runtime-incident | Yes for Sev1 |
| Customer Comms & RCA | CSM & Support coordinate status updates and timeline | CSM | Support Eng | #cs-updates | No |

- Communication Templates (use verbatim in customer comms):
  - Initial Acknowledgement: "We are investigating increased error rates affecting inference for your account. Our team will provide an update within 60 minutes. Severity: {Sev}."
  - Status Update: "Root cause: {short summary}. Mitigation in place: {mitigation}. ETA for full resolution: {ETA}."
  - Postmortem Summary: include timeline, impact, root cause, long-term fix, and customer-facing mitigations.

Integration Guides (common customer environments):
- AWS (VPC + PrivateLink):
  - Requirements: Allowlist endpoints: api.redwood.ai (Hosted) or customer-dedicated-endpoint; ensure TLS 1.2+, mutual TLS if configured.
  - Sample security group rules (egress):
    - Type: HTTPS, Destination: api.redwood.ai, Port: 443, Description: Redwood API
  - Test command: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health

- Azure (VNet Integration):
  - Ensure route tables and NSGs allow outbound connectivity to Redwood endpoints.
  - Service endpoints for Private deployments require subnet-level configuration.

- On‑Prem / Air‑Gapped:
  - Follow onprem-packaging guide and KMS/HSM key exchange process. In-person validation and packaging checks required before go‑live.

Known Issues & Workarounds (curated list):
1) Intermittent 502s during traffic bursts (Hosted):
- Symptoms: Short spikes of 502 errors at p99 traffic bursts.
- Root cause (common): Transient autoscaling delays or backend kernel warmup.
- Workaround: Apply client-side retry with exponential backoff (max 3 retries) and jitter; enable short-term queuing on client at peak.

2) Streaming stalls on token boundary for long responses:
- Symptoms: Streaming stops sending tokens for ~2–5s intermittently.
- Workaround: Fall back to non-streaming request pattern for affected prompt templates, or reduce max_tokens per request. SE to capture traces and open runtime bug if reproducible.

3) Embedding quality regressions after model roll (Hosted):
- Symptoms: Semantic similarity score drift for a known prompt set.
- Workaround: Pin to a previously verified model variant for the customer; coordinate model rollback with Product via support escalation.

Support Process & SLAs:
- For enterprise customers we guarantee priority handling per contract. Standard internal SLOs for support response: initial ack for Sev1 within 15 minutes, for Sev2 within 30 minutes.
- Operational artifacts to enable:
  - Shared support Slack channel or PagerDuty escalation contact.
  - Access to relevant dashboards: per-customer latency/cost breakdown, per-route error rates, and token usage.

Health Checks & QBR Material:
- Weekly health check (first 8 weeks):
  - Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, errors per 1k requests, tokens per request, cost per 1k tokens, cache hit ratio, KV cache miss rate.
  - Actions: identify regressions, confirm model/quantization profile in use, review throttles and quota alerts.

- Monthly health check (ongoing):
  - High-level metric review + action items logged in the account JIRA.

- QBR cadence & sample agenda (quarterly):
  - 1) Wins & adoption metrics (usage, features adopted)
  - 2) Reliability review (SLOs, incidents, remediation status)
  - 3) Performance & cost optimizations (batching, quantization suggestions)
  - 4) Roadmap alignment & feature requests
  - 5) Action items & owners

- QBR Template (to attach to meeting notes):
| Section | Data to include | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Executive Summary | Top 3 highlights, top 3 risks | CSM |
| Usage & Adoption | Monthly active endpoints, tokens/month, peak RPS | CSM/SE |
| Reliability | Incidents this quarter, Mean Time To Restore (MTTR) | Support |
| Cost Efficiency | Cost per 1k tokens, optimizations applied | Finance/CSM |
| Roadmap Requests | Customer asks mapped to product tickets | Product/SE |

Templates & Artifacts (links to shared drive / templates):
- Onboarding checklist (link to template): /drive/templates/enterprise-onboarding-checklist.xlsx
- QBR deck template: /drive/templates/qbr-deck.pptx
- Incident postmortem template: /drive/templates/incident-postmortem.md

Operational Runbooks & Tools:
- Dashboards: /dashboards/customer/<account-id> - includes per-route latency, cost, and embedding quality checks.
- Logs & Traces: Use centralized tracing: tracer.redwood.internal -> retrieval command: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" https://tracer.redwood.internal/api/search?account={account-id}
- PagerDuty runbook: Escalation names and oncall schedule lives in PagerDuty (service: Redwood-Customer-Support).

Postmortem & RCA Guidelines:
- Required fields: impact statement, timeline (minute granularity), root cause, mitigation, long-term fix, customer communication, owners, and ETA.
- Publish within 72 hours of Sev1 resolution to the #postmortems channel and link to customer JIRA.

Appendix: Sample Quick Commands
- Health endpoint test: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health | jq
- Simple inference smoke test: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"prompt":"Hello","max_tokens":10}'

notes: Use this playbook as the canonical onboarding artifact. Update reviewers and labels when major process changes occur. For Private deployments follow eng-private-deployments/onprem-packaging for packaging-specific checks.
